text:
sam: FYI we have Sirocco on a Dedicated pool (d-pool-42) reporting 429s and p95s spiking ~2–3x during their campaign window starting 2026-03-12 05:00 UTC. Customer says baseline QPS 60, peak bursts ~280 for ~10m. They attached request IDs; I collected some server logs.

clare: Can you paste the sample request IDs and the pool config? I want to check slab sizing + autoscale policy.

sam: Request ids: r=fb1a9c, r=fb1a9d, r=fb1aa3 (timestamps 05:02–05:11). Pool: d-pool-42, reserved_slabs=2, slab_gpu=V100x8, min_instances=2, max_instances=6, scale_policy=cpu_and_qps, cooldown=300s. Customer notes they saw retries from their side which might have amplified load.

anya: Looking at metrics — their baseline 60 qps maps to ~25% util on 2 slabs during steady state, but the 280 qps bursts push util > 90% before autoscale completes. Autoscale ramp is ~4m to add 2 instances in our current policy. That explains tail latency and some 429s while warmups happen.

mike: Also noticing occasional auth refresh failures in the logs around the same time, e.g.:
```
2026-03-12T05:03:14Z d-pool-42 auth: token_refresh_error user=sirocco-client code=401 duration=12ms
2026-03-12T05:03:17Z d-pool-42 serve: request_id=fb1a9d status=429 reason=rate_limit instance=x-02 p95=610ms
```
Possible double-effect: clients retry on 401/429 leading to higher instantaneous qps.

clare: Could be noisy-neighbor + auth flapping. Do we have tenant throttling logs? Is the 429 from our global throttler or per-tenant slab limiter?

sam: 429s are showing "tenant_slab_exceeded" in a subset and "global_queue_full" in others — looks like two failure modes. I asked the customer for their retry policy.

support-bot: Attached: customer_retry_policy.txt (they use exponential backoff starting at 200ms, max 3 retries).

anya: With 200ms initial backoff and lots of in-flight retries, bursts can amplify by ~1.4x in practice. For d-pool-42, warmup plus amplification pushes us beyond max_instances for ~2–6 minutes.

mike: Repro plan I ran locally against a staging replica: steady baseline 60 qps + synthetic burst to 300 qps for 10m with retry=3. Observed autoscale delay ~3.5m, p95 up to 720ms, 429s during ramp. I posted the repro harness in #eng-runtime.

clare: Short term mitigation suggestions: 1) bump reserved_slabs to 3 (immediate capacity), 2) increase min_instances to 3 and reduce scale cooldown to 120s so autoscale reacts faster, 3) enable request-level token bucket for this tenant to smooth bursts (if product OK). Any objections?

sam: Customer asked about billing — they saw unexpectedly high billed tokens during the window because retries counted. They want a credit if we confirm platform-side contribution.

anya: We should confirm accounting: if retries were because of 401 token refresh failures on our auth proxy, that's our fault and we should refund redundant tokens in that window. If retries were client-side only, still consider a partial credit since warmup/autoscale contributed. I can extract counts per request_id.

mike: Quick actions I've queued:
- scaled d-pool-42 reserved_slabs: 2 -> 3 (effective now)
- set min_instances: 2 -> 3
- scale.cooldown: 300s -> 120s (for next 2 hours)
I also triggered a controlled warmup by seeding cached KV for the model (to reduce cold-init).

eng-oncall-bot: Deploy change to d-pool-42 config accepted; will revert cooldown after 2h.

clare: Medium-term: recommend customer moves to a larger committed slab or schedule a warmup window before marketing blasts. Also we should add an "auth-retry-safe" guidance to our docs for dedicated customers that explains how auth refresh failures interact with retries and autoscale.

sam: Customer requested repro steps we used. Mike, can you paste the minimal curl sequence/locally-run harness so they can self-verify after config changes?

mike: Minimal repro (staging):
```bash
# baseline 60 qps for 30m, then burst 300 qps for 10m with 3 retries
python3 tools/harness.py --target https://staging-infer.redwood.ai --baseline 60 --burst 300 --burst-duration 600 --retries 3
```
Or single-request test to trigger auth:
```bash
curl -i -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" \\
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \\
  -d '{"model":"rwd-13b", "input":"test"}'
```

anya: I've exported per-request token accounting for the suspected window and will attach CSV to ticket. If counts show extra tokens tied to server 401s, support → billing credit.

sam: Customer is OK with the immediate changes; they're scheduling another campaign in 48h. Please keep this thread for follow-ups and paste the final billing decision.

clare: I'll follow up with a short runbook for customers on Dedicated: recommended min_instances, retry guidance, and warmup checklist. I'll also open a small runtime task to handle faster scale ramp for slab-limited pools.

support-bot: Ticket updated: INC-2026-9983 linked, customer notified of temporary capacity bump and pending billing review. :white_check_mark:

mike: TL;DR: root cause = underprovisioned slab for observed burst profile + auth refresh churn amplifying retries; mitigations=instant slab bump, raise min_instances, faster cooldown, warmup, billing review.

sam: Thanks team. I'll close once billing confirms credit and customer verifies improved latency in next run. :thumbsup:
